Perform a targeted web search to identify theses (2010–2020 inclusive) that discuss sustainable coolant alternatives used in machining. Focus on keywords: "thesis" OR "dissertation" + ("minimum quantity lubrication" OR MQL OR "vegetable oil" OR biodegradable OR eco-friendly OR sustainable OR cryogenic OR CO2 OR LN2 OR nanofluid) + machining + (aluminum OR aluminium OR brass OR copper OR bronze OR titanium). For each candidate, collect: thesis title, author, year, university, coolant type discussed, alloy(s) machined, machining process (turning/milling/drilling/grinding), link to thesis or repository. Limit initial list to ~15 strongest candidates across different universities. Where available, note if the thesis includes a biographical section stating the author’s B.Sc completion year (we need 2005–2013). Also note any immediate clues on the university’s 19th-century (1850s) student enrollment growth from official university history pages or Wikipedia for later verification. Return a structured summary of candidates.

Comprehensive Summary and Final Answer Task overview - Goal: Identify the exact thesis title (2010–2020 inclusive) that: 1) Discusses a coolant that has emerged as a sustainable alternative used in machining (e.g., MQL, cryogenic CO2/LN2, eco-friendly fluids). 2) Machines an alloy with annealing temperature >300°C and <800°C, and modulus of elasticity >10,000 ksi and <18,000 ksi (≈68.9–124 GPa). 3) Was produced at a university whose student numbers increased rapidly in the 1850s. 4) Has an author who completed a B.Sc degree between 2005–2013 inclusive. - Deliverable: Name of the thesis title, plus a transparent, complete report of all plausible candidates identified, evidence, reasoning, uncertainties, and intermediate findings. Approach and reasoning highlights - Interpreted “sustainable coolant” to include minimum quantity lubrication (MQL), cryogenic LN2/CO2, and other eco-friendly or reduced-consumption metalworking approaches. - Focused alloy property window (E ≈ 68.9–124 GPa; anneal 300–800°C) suggests aluminum alloys and many titanium alloys are good candidates; steels are typically excluded (E ≈ 200 GPa). - The “1850s rapid student increase” strongly points to older European institutions founded mid-19th century (not recently founded universities). ETH Zurich (founded 1855) has documented early rapid growth. - Conducted incremental web-research subtasks to find theses across multiple repositories, then validated candidates against all constraints, including author B.Sc year and university historical data. Working history and web-research subtasks (concise) 1) Initial discovery (Shodhganga repository, India) - Targeted searches for “minimum quantity lubrication” and machining topics yielded: - Effect of Minimum Quantity Lubrication Technique on Machining Characteristics of Ductile Material during Face Milling (Kamaljeet Singh, 2020, Chitkara University). Link: https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/10603/301845 - Study on Influence of Nano Additives in Minimum Quantity Lubrication System Used in Metal Cutting Operation (R. Anburaj, Completed 2017, Pondicherry University). Link: https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/10603/293870 - Investigations on drilling of CFRP Ti6Al4V stacks under dry and MQL (Prabukarthi A, 2018, Anna University). Link: https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/10603/303656 - Experimental investigations on performance of nano cutting fluids with graphite inclusions in MQL (Rama M M S Prasad, 2017). Link: https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/10603/135249 - Constraints check: These institutions are predominantly 20th/21st century foundations; thus they likely fail the “1850s rapid student growth” criterion. Alloy specifics and B.Sc years were not visible on landing pages; PDFs not fully reviewed there. 2) Expansion to UK repositories (White Rose eTheses, University of Sheffield) - Identified strong theses involving sustainable coolants and alloys meeting property windows: - Subsurface deformation micromechanisms induced during machining of titanium alloys at low temperatures, and a novel testing methodology to examine their machining behaviour (Maureen Aceves, 2019). Link: https://etheses.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/23100/ • Discusses cryogenic cooling (LN2/CO2) and MQL for machining Ti-6Al-4V ELI (E ≈ 114 GPa; anneal ≈ 700–760°C). Fails 1850s university clue (University of Sheffield founded 1905). - Machining Fibre Metal Laminates and Al2024-T3 aluminium alloy (Khaled Giasin, 2017). Link: https://etheses.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/16061/ • Uses LN2 and MQL in drilling aluminum and GLARE laminates. Aluminum 2024-T3 fits property window (E ≈ 73 GPa; anneal ≈ 325–495°C). Fails 1850s university clue. 3) Focused search and verification at ETH Zurich (founded 1855; early rapid growth) - Identified ETH theses (2010–2020): - Developing Metalworking Fluids for Titanium Cutting (Linus Meier, 2020). Link: https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/entities/publication/0b394832-b712-4b65-9c81-a8d40c181982 - Fluid Supply in Cylindrical Grinding (Christoph Baumgart, 2020). Link: https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/entities/publication/305c2853-0894-4e1b-af6a-6bf68852803f - High Performance Dry Grinding – HPDG (Michal Kuffa, 2017). Link: https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/entities/publication/86c0e55b-273b-491a-bfcf-c6994ff83ec0 - Rounded cutting edges and their influence in machining titanium (Carl-Frederik Wyen, 2011; restricted). Link: https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/entities/publication/d3427519-84b0-40be-aa81-109cbf082f7c Candidate set with constraint alignment - Shodhganga candidates (2017–2020): - Sustainable coolants (MQL/nanofluids) present; alloys and B.Sc generally unverified on landing pages. - University 1850s growth: Not applicable (modern institutions). - Status: Plausible for coolant/alloy but rejected due to failing 1850s criterion. - University of Sheffield (2017, 2019): - Strong matches for sustainable coolants and alloy properties (Ti-6Al-4V; Al2024-T3). - University 1850s growth: Fails (founded 1905). - Status: Strong but rejected due to 1850s criterion. - ETH Zurich (2011, 2017, 2020): - University 1850s growth: Likely satisfied (founded 1855 with documented early influx of students). - Developing Metalworking Fluids for Titanium Cutting (Meier, 2020): Strong match on all constraints (details below). - Fluid Supply in Cylindrical Grinding (Baumgart, 2020): Focus on coolant supply/minimization; alloy unspecified; likely steels—property window uncertain. - High Performance Dry Grinding – HPDG (Kuffa, 2017): Emphasizes dry grinding; alloy unclear (likely steels), outside modulus window; weaker fit. - Rounded Cutting Edges… (Wyen, 2011): Titanium machining focus; coolant alternative not central and restricted access; weaker evidentiary fit. Detailed verification of the strongest candidate: Linus Meier (2020, ETH Zurich) Thesis: Developing Metalworking Fluids for Titanium Cutting - Item page: https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/entities/publication/0b394832-b712-4b65-9c81-a8d40c181982 - PDF: https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/server/api/core/bitstreams/eea5f353-c85a-4997-9c7f-93dfb9ccac76/content 1) Coolant as “sustainable alternative” (MQL, cryogenic CO2/LN2) - “In most cases however, MWFs have to compete against dry cutting, minimum quantity lubrication (MQL), and cryogenic cooling.” (p.18) - “In recent years, more emphasis is put on ecologically sustainable metal cutting… With the current trend to minimize metalworking usage with MQL… The polar ester bond… makes vegetable oils ideal for MQL fluids.” (p.28) - “Emulsion spray and cryogenic gases were able to penetrate much further… showed a lower coefficient of friction for MQL than for flood cooling…” (p.26) - “According to a review of Ezugwu et al. [51] in 2003 cryogenic cooling has the potential to reduce tool wear below the level of flood cooling… later confirmed by Deiab et al. [44].” (p.35) - “…reduction in adhesive properties when reducing the temperature with liquid nitrogen.” (p.44) 2) Alloy and machining processes - Alloy: “The titanium alloy Ti6Al4V (Titanium Grade 5) is chosen since it is the most prevalent in titanium cutting…” (p.55) - Processes: Turning and milling - “In full scale turning tests…”; “…In full scale milling tests… single-fluted milling tools.” (p.16) - “A NLX 4000/750 CNC lathe by DMG Mori… is used in all turning tests.” (p.50) - Dedicated milling test sections (pp.67–80; e.g., 5.5.2 Single-Flute Finish Milling Tests; 5.5.3 Single-Flute Rough Milling Tests) 3) Alloy property verification for Ti‑6Al‑4V (Grade 5) - Modulus and annealing from AZoM datasheet (authoritative technical source) - Link: https://www.azom.com/article.aspx?ArticleID=1547 - “Elastic Modulus GPa (Msi) 114 (17)” → 114 GPa ≈ 17,000 ksi (within 10,000–18,000 ksi). - “Annealing - 732°C (1350°F), 4hr…” → 732°C (within 300–800°C). 4) Author’s B.Sc completion year (2005–2013 inclusive) - Thesis CV/front matter: - “Academic studies 2009–2012 BSc Mechanical Engineering, ETH Zurich; 2012–2014 MSc…” (p.196) - Conclusion: B.Sc completion year is 2012 (within target window). 5) University historical clue: 1850s rapid increase in student numbers - ETH Zurich official history (1855–1904): https://ethz.ch/en/the-eth-zurich/portrait/history/epochs/1855-1904.html - “In the early years, the Federal Polytechnic School benefited from the repressive climate that prevailed at other European polytechnic institutions. Students flocked to Zurich from all over Europe, attracted by the newly appointed professors…” (ETH official wording; “students flocked” ≈ rapid increase in the 1850s/early years) Constraint satisfaction summary for Linus Meier (2020) - Time window (2010–2020): Yes (2020). - Sustainable coolant discussed and used in machining: Yes (MQL and cryogenic LN2/CO2; explicit sustainability context). - Alloy property window: Yes (Ti‑6Al‑4V E ≈ 17,000 ksi; anneal ≈ 732°C). - University 1850s growth: Yes (ETH 1855 founding; official history describes early years with students “flocking” to Zurich). - Author B.Sc in 2005–2013: Yes (B.Sc completed in 2012). Other candidates and why they were not selected - Maureen Aceves (2019, Univ. of Sheffield): Strong match on coolants and alloy (Ti‑6Al‑4V; cryogenic/MQL), but University of Sheffield was founded in 1905 (no 1850s student growth). Link: https://etheses.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/23100/ - Khaled Giasin (2017, Univ. of Sheffield): Strong match on LN2/MQL and Al2024-T3 (properties fit), but fails the 1850s criterion.
